parsed.rationale: The cluster groups 16 distinct `type-alias-object` records whose only shared structural signal is `shared_field_count: 1` (i.e., all are empty-body type aliases) and whose names are entirely unrelated domain concepts: `ConfettiView`, `DebugHUD`, `DialADJPage`, `HeightReader`, `InfoDetailView`, `PlaycutLoadingSection`, `TalksetView`, `WXYCLogo`, etc. Each alias lives in a different package (`DebugPanel`, `WXUI`, `Wallpaper`, `PartyHorn`, `PlayerHeaderView`, `MusicShareKit`, `app:WatchXYC`, `app:iOS`) and wraps a locally meaningful SwiftUI view type. The structural coincidence is purely that Swift type aliases have no body — there is no shared semantic content to extract, consolidate, or generalize. Merging or lifting these aliases would couple unrelated packages around a meaningless structural artifact.
